page_placements.theme: Weight edits can remove refusal incompletely (single rank-1 passes, skipped residual writers, low-bit edits)

record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README and a truncated file list only; code was not read or run. The file list says 404 files, but only the first 400 are shown.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports a live rank-1 abliteration on Qwen2.5-0.5B and a change in refusal margin. It does not establish the original activation-projection procedure or report refusal behavior rates, so this is a conceptual test rather than a direct reproduction.
record.gate_note: The README reports a refusal-margin change after a single surgical pass. Layer separability and projection quantities are described as diagnostic outputs, but no separate results for them are given; values used to select a layer are not recorded. General claims about capabilities being preserved by orthogonality are not empirical capability results.
record.test_reason: This is a tool repository. It takes the Arditi et al. direction as given and implements abliteration. Its only reported number is its own pipeline's effect on an internal 'refusal margin' (13.93 to 7.03 on Qwen2.5-0.5B). That is a representation-level score, not a refusal or compliance rate. There is no capability evaluation, no induction by adding the direction, and no released-model behaviour check. It reports its own method's performance without a behavioural result on any version, so it does not test the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The README treats refusal as a near-linear direction, citing Arditi et al. 2024. It says abliteration removes only the rank-1 component, so capabilities are 'preserved' by construction. It calls the Qwen2.5-0.5B margin drop (13.93 to 7.03) 'verified end-to-end'. No behavioural refusal rates or capability benchmarks are reported for this example.
record.recipe_differences: Tool repo, not a replication. It describes rank-1 abliteration informed by harmful/harmless separability, but does not state the full direction-extraction and intervention procedure or report the original behavioral measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The README describes layer-specific separability and identifies a peak layer, but gives no results comparing layers or other settings.

fits_no_version.finding: One rank-1 weight-orthogonalization pass on Qwen2.5-0.5B lowers the peak-layer harmful/harmless refusal margin from 13.93 to 7.03, so about half the margin remains.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A single directional weight edit only partly collapses the activation-level harmful/harmless separation at the peak layer.

record.problems: The sole reported result is for one model and one pass; no controls or uncertainty are reported. The refusal-margin change does not establish refusal removal, and the claim of preserved capabilities is not backed by a reported capability evaluation.
record.rows_left_out: No separate results are reported for layer profiles or projection quantities; the README describes these as diagnostic outputs used to locate or characterize the edit. General test-suite counts are not results on the claim.

untested.parts: Refusal/compliance rates after ablation, inducing refusal by adding the direction, and empirical capability retention. The README asserts capabilities are 'preserved' by orthogonality but reports no evaluation.
Behavioural refusal after the weight edit. Only an activation margin is reported.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' and its V1 limits_scope label are removed. The margin is a confidence/separability-style score, not the behaviour itself, and comes from the tool's own pipeline. The repo includes lm-eval and safety-suite loaders, plus modules for multiple directions and subspaces, but reports no results from them. Code was not read.

versions.untested_parts: The reported result is a refusal-margin change, not a refusal/compliance rate. The README does not report adding the direction, an all-layer-and-position activation projection, or an empirical check that other capabilities remain intact.
Although the README describes weight editing and abliteration, it does not report refusal behavior after a weight edit in released models.
No results on attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
Multiple refusal directions are listed as a tool feature, but no results compare one direction with an affine, cone, or multi-direction account.
No results separate harmfulness judgment from refusal decision.
No cross-language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer results.
No results vary refusal training or its timing.
